entries.summary: Information in an annual tax performance report is not subject to the tax confidentiality provisions of RCW 82.32.330 and may be disclosed to the public upon request.

entries.summary: No county, city, town or other municipal corporation may give money or property, or loan its money or credit, to or in aid of any individual, association, company or corporation, except for the necessary support of the poor and infirm.
entries.text: No county, city, town or other municipal corporation shall hereafter give any money, or property, or loan its money, or credit to or in aid of any individual, association, company or corporation, except for the necessary support of the poor and infirm, or become directly or indirectly the owner of any stock in or bonds of any association, company or corporation.

source.citation: Washington Constitution art. VIII, § 7

entries.notes: A public utility district is a municipal corporation. The Municipal Research and Services Center states that under this provision a local government may not directly give or loan money to private businesses for economic development. Article VIII, Section 10 creates an express exception permitting utilities to provide conservation assistance, which indicates the general prohibition reaches utilities. A Washington Attorney General opinion concluded that a municipal utility loaning funds to its own customers is not saved by a long-range benefit to the utility. Public utility districts are not subject to rate regulation by the Utilities and Transportation Commission, and the rate discrimination bar at RCW 80.28.100 reaches gas, electrical and water companies rather than districts.
entries.confidence_note: The constitutional text is read in original. The identification of this provision as the basis for a Grant County PUD manager's statement that public utilities are barred from offering better rates to a particular class is DERIVED and is not stated in any source read. Whether a differential rate that still recovers cost of service would constitute a gift has not been researched and is a question for counsel. entries.summary: A business or tenant claiming the data center sales and use tax exemption must file an annual tax performance report that identifies construction firm names and employment levels used for constructing, renovating, refurbishing or remodeling the data centers.
entries.text: A qualifying business or a qualifying tenant claiming an exemption under this section or RCW 82.12.986 must complete an annual tax performance report with the department as required under RCW 82.32.534. The report must identify construction firm names and employment levels used for constructing, renovating, refurbishing, or remodeling the data centers.

source.citation: RCW 82.08.986(6), app.leg.wa.gov

entries.notes: The contractor-naming duty sits in the exemption statute itself, not in RCW 82.32.534, which is the general annual tax performance report provision. Under 82.32.534 the report is due by May 31 of the year following the calendar year in which the preference was claimed, beginning in calendar year 2018, and must detail employment by total number of full-time, part-time and temporary positions. Employee names are excluded. A filer may instead authorize the Employment Security Department to release the same employment and wage data. Related: RCW 82.08.986 and 82.12.986 establish the exemption for eligible server equipment and power infrastructure in rural counties; RCW 82.08.9861 governs the 2022 program, barring new certificates on or after July 1 2028, with exemptions expiring July 1 2038 and a qualifying tenant minimum of 150 kW contracted.
entries.confidence_note: Statute read in original at the point cited. Whether ESSB 6231, chapter 266 Laws of 2026, alters the reporting duty has not been checked. No filed report has been obtained, so what the reports actually contain is unestablished.
